Consult Summary:
- 28-year-old woman with new-onset left-sided posterior throbbing headache since yesterday (8/10), no focal neurologic or systemic red-flag symptoms, minimally responsive to ibuprofen; advised stronger NSAID (not ibuprofen) with food, acetaminophen adjunct, rest/hydration, and strict return precautions if worsening or not resolving within 1–2 days.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Headache.
- Location: Left posterior/occipital region.
- Character: Throbbing; initially intense; built up gradually over a short period.
- Severity: 8/10.
- Onset: Mid-morning yesterday.
- Course: Persistent since onset; unusual for her (no prior similar headaches).
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: No change with position (lying down/standing), bending over, coughing/sneezing; ibuprofen (Nurofen) yesterday provided no significant relief; sleep unaffected (slept through the night).
- Associated symptoms:
  - Denies nausea, vomiting.
  - Denies tingling, numbness, weakness.
  - Denies blurred vision, eye pain, photophobia, visual phenomena (“funny lights”).
  - Denies fever, chills/shivers, sweats.
  - Denies rash.
  - Eating and drinking as normal.
- Impact: Has not missed work but finds it hard to perform work/normal activities.
- Other: Blood pressure not checked recently.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions reported.
- Denies asthma and stomach problems.
- Medications:
  - None regularly.
  - Recent OTC: Ibuprofen (Nurofen) taken yesterday; dose/route/frequency not documented; minimal effect.
- Allergies: No drug allergies reported by patient.

Social History:
- Lives with partner.
- Occupation: Designer.
- Tobacco: Never smoker.
- Alcohol: Denies regular use.
- Recreational drugs: Denies use.
- Functional status: Difficulty carrying out normal tasks due to headache; no days missed from work.

Family History:
- Mother: Hypertension; migraines.

Physical Examination:
- Not documented.

Investigations:
- None performed or documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute new-onset unilateral throbbing headache without red-flag symptoms
  - Assessment: Left-sided posterior throbbing headache since yesterday; severe (8/10); no focal neurologic deficits or systemic symptoms elicited; first notable headache for patient; poor response to single dose of ibuprofen.
  - Plan:
    - Analgesia: Stronger NSAID prescribed; name/dose/route/frequency not documented. Instruction to use instead of ibuprofen and not concurrently; take regularly with food.
    - May take acetaminophen (paracetamol) alongside the prescribed NSAID as adjunct analgesia.
    - Supportive care: Rest and maintain good hydration.
    - Safety-netting/return precautions: Seek care if pain worsens, new symptoms develop (fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness), or if similar episodes recur.
    - Follow-up: If not improving or not settling within 1–2 days after starting prescribed medication, contact clinic for reassessment.

- General plan items:
  - None additional documented.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vital signs; neurologic exam (including cranial nerves, motor/sensory, gait); fundoscopic exam; pregnancy status; exact medication name and dosing instructions for prescribed NSAID; explicit allergy confirmation documentation; problem list and medication reconciliation.
- Internal conflicts: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor filler words; no significant audio issues reported.
